criterion_notes.c1: The abstract and opening introduction explicitly examine domestic urban water supply systems and household/locality water accessibility and distribution in non-municipal areas of Shillong, India.
criterion_notes.c2: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the abstract and introduction indicate that the paper examines formal (municipal) and informal (non-municipal, dorbar shnong) local institutional water governance, which points toward yes under broad institutional/governance wording. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading, municipal versus non-municipal institutional/regulatory governance of domestic water distribution could potentially qualify if the study analyzes specific institutional structure, eligibility/locality rules, tariffs, discretion, or allocation rules directly governing access rather than generic governance background; however, because the retrieved PDF is only a 2-page publisher preview (pp. 251-252 of 251-277) cutting off mid-sentence in Section 1, Criterion 2 cannot be verified from the available text.
criterion_notes.c3: Unclear because only pages 251-252 of a 27-page article (pp. 251-277) are present in the retrieved PDF, cutting off mid-sentence in the Introduction before any methods or empirical data are presented.
criterion_notes.c4: The abstract states that the article uses indicators of quantity, quality, accessibility, and reliability and examines domestic water distribution and inequity, but actual outcome measures and results are missing from the truncated 2-page preview.
criterion_notes.c5: Study design, sampling, unit of analysis, operationalized exposure, and reported outcomes cannot be verified because pages 253-277 are absent from the retrieved 2-page preview PDF.
